Dear Viking,

please do not hijack old threads that are unrelated to your question.
It is like if a librarian would put books backs in random locations
making it hard for others.

On Fri, Jun 25, 2010 at 9:40 AM, Liang Cheng <vikin...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Henrik,
> I read your file aroma.affymetrix :Analysis of small to very large
> Affymetrix data sets. In page 25, we have to know the chip type in order to
> read the raw data. How can I know the chip type? Currently I know that my
> chip type is 250k and there are two types of 250K chips.

You can simply try to load the data. If the CEL files are not of the
chip type you think, then aroma.affymetrix will tell you what it has
detected. For example, assume you have a data set named
Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal that you *think* have Mapping250K_Sty CEL
files. Then you place those in:

rawData/Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/Mapping250K_Sty/

The try to load it as:

library("aroma.affymetrix");
csR <- AffymetrixCelSet$byName("Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal",
chipType="Mapping250K_Sty");

If the CEL files is of a different chip type than Mapping250K_Sty,
then you will get an error telling you what it finds, e.g.

Error in list(`AffymetrixCelSet$byName("Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal", chipType =
"Mapping2` = <environment>, :

[2010-07-02 00:00:09] Exception: Invalid name of directory containing
CEL files. The name of the directory (Mapping250K_Sty) must be the
same as the chip type used for the CEL files (Mapping250K_Nsp) unless
using argument 'checkChipType=FALSE':
rawData/Affymetrix_2006-TumorNormal/Mapping250K_Sty

Hope this helps

Henrik
